**A chunk should contain enough evidence to answer a question without burying that evidence in unrelated material.** Fixed token windows are predictable but can split a definition from its qualifier. Overlap reduces boundary loss while duplicating text and increasing index size. [1](https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401)

Recursive splitting respects paragraphs and headings until a size limit. Structure-aware splitting keeps tables or sections intact with parent metadata. Semantic splitting groups related sentences, but similarity alone may still separate a rule from a necessary exception.

**Consider a policy paragraph followed by “except for temporary staff.”** Retrieving only the first paragraph can produce a confident wrong answer. Parent expansion or contextual metadata may be more useful than simply increasing every chunk size.

Contextual retrieval adds a short document-specific description before indexing. Preserve the original passage and provenance so generated context does not become unsupported evidence. Compare answer-bearing recall, citation correctness, final grounded accuracy, latency, and storage. Tune chunking with reranking and context budget; a fact lookup and a cross-section synthesis need different evidence granularity.

**Technical details and references.**

Fixed token windows are cheap and predictable but split arguments and tables; overlap reduces boundary loss while duplicating evidence. Recursive splitting respects paragraph/heading boundaries until a size limit. Structure-aware chunks preserve sections, tables, and parent metadata. Semantic splitting groups related sentences but adds embedding cost and can still separate necessary definitions. [1](https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401)

Contextual retrieval prepends a short document-specific explanation before indexing each chunk; keep original text and provenance so generated context cannot silently become evidence. Compare alternatives on answer-bearing retrieval recall, grounded answer accuracy, citation correctness, index size, and latency. Tune chunk size jointly with reranking and context budgets. There is no universally optimal chunk length: a short factual lookup and a cross-section synthesis require different evidence granularity.
